papers.title: SegJointGene: joint cell segmentation and spatial gene prioritization by information entropy guided convolutional neural networks
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Spatial sequencing technologies enable the single-cell-level study of molecular organization in tissues. Revealing such spatial patterns relies on accurate cell segmentation. In complex tissues with dense cell packing, segmentation based solely on nuclear staining is insufficient for accurate cell boundary detection. This limitation arises because accurate segmentation necessitates the delineation of cell morphology, which is driven by molecular activities such as cytoskeletal dynamics, cell-cell adhesion, and intercellular signaling. Thus, integrating molecular information, including gene or protein expression, has the potential to improve segmentation, but remains computationally challenging. Results To address this, we developed SegJointGene, a deep learning framework that jointly performs cell segmentation and spatial gene prioritization by integrating nuclei-based images with spatial gene or protein expression data. SegJointGene designs an information-entropy–guided convolutional neural network together with a computational information discarding score to identify genes that are important for cell-type–specific segmentation. The model iteratively refines gene prioritization and cell boundaries, producing convergent segmentation results along with prioritized spatial genes or proteins across cell types. We applied and benchmarked SegJointGene on both simulation and real spatial datasets, including spatial transcriptomics from the mouse hippocampus and distinct regions of the whole mouse brain, as well as spatial proteomics data from human tonsil. Across datasets, SegJointGene outperformed existing methods by 5–20% in accurately assigning molecular signals to cell boundaries. Robustness analyses further demonstrated stable performance across varying gene numbers and imaging resolutions. In addition, the genes prioritized by SegJointGene were enriched for structural, developmental, and synaptic signaling pathways, supporting their relevance to spatial tissue organization. Availability The source code and data are available at https://github.com/daifengwanglab/segjointgene

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
空间序列技术使得在单细胞水平上研究组织中的分子结构成为可能。要揭示这些空间模式，准确的细胞分割是必不可少的。然而，在细胞密度较高的复杂组织中，仅依靠核染色进行细胞分割并不足以精确确定细胞边界——因为准确的细胞分割需要同时考虑细胞的形态特征，而这些特征又受到细胞骨架动态、细胞间黏附以及细胞信号传导等分子过程的影响。因此，整合基因或蛋白质表达等分子信息确实有助于提升分割精度，但这一过程在计算上仍面临巨大挑战。  

**研究方法**  
为了解决这一问题，我们开发了SegJointGene这一深度学习框架。该框架通过将基于核染色的图像数据与空间基因/蛋白质表达信息相结合，同时完成细胞分割和基因优先级排序的任务。SegJointGene采用信息熵引导的卷积神经网络，并结合特定的计算算法来识别对细胞类型特异性分割具有重要作用的基因。该模型通过迭代优化基因优先级及细胞边界信息，最终能够生成一致的分割结果，并确定不同细胞类型中具有关键作用的分子靶标。我们在模拟数据集以及真实的空间生物学数据集上对SegJointGene进行了测试——这些数据包括来自小鼠海马区及整个大脑各区域的转录组学数据，以及人类扁桃体的蛋白质组学数据。结果表明，在将分子信号准确分配给细胞边界的任务中，SegJointGene的性能比现有方法高出5%至20%；此外，其稳定性也得到了验证——无论基因数量或成像分辨率如何变化，该模型的性能均保持稳定。进一步分析还发现，SegJointGene所优先识别的基因主要涉及结构、发育及突触信号传导相关通路，这进一步证明了这些基因与组织空间结构的形成密切相关。  

**数据与代码获取方式**  
源代码及相关数据可访问以下链接：  
https://github.com/daifengwanglab/segjointgene
